articles.title: The rise of 'housefishing' - when does using AI go from enhancing to misleading?
articles.description: Experts warn that using AI to enhance property images can go too far and mislead prospective buyers.
articles.summary: The images Olivia Nicole saw of a home on Rightmove (l) were completely different to how the property looked in real life (r) Have you ever been impressed by the pictures of a property on an estate agent's website, only to find the place looks completely different when you view…
key_points: Then there's a chance that AI was used to enhance the images you saw.
From repainted walls to imaginary lawns, estate agents are increasingly using the technology to make homes seem more appealing, arguing it helps buyers visualise the potential of a place.
But experts warn it can go too far and mislead prospective buyers - a trend dubbed "housefishing".

Milburn, a former Labour health secretary, has been tasked by the government with helping reduce the one in eight 18- to 24-year-olds in the UK who are not in education, employment or training…
